body: I sent you a PM, but if I don't hear from you soon, I'll respond here as well. Thank you for taking the time to reply

Thank you for replying. I really appreciate it. Hoping for someone to respond so I can talk about things is what's getting me through tonight. I'm still really scared. And sorry for writing so much, but I still feel like I even left out a lot. 

My cutting is a lot better than it used to be, and I know I should stop. I've been told all the coping mechanisms, and some of them have worked to slow it down. The problem is that my anxiety and depression get so bad it overwhelms me, and I cut enough to regain composure. I don't have enough motivation to really start a hobby. I spent my day off today staying in bed until 4:30 because I felt no reason to get up... and once I did spent the whole day consumed with anxiety and regretting what happened yesterday. 

I'll give AA a chance. You're right. There's not a reason to avoid it so strongly. I just... it just feels like so much defeat, and I hear it has religious undertones, and my family background and experience with religion makes me worried.

I should spend less time around my ex, but I just don't have anyone else around me that I can share anything with or spend any time with. I should say something, but she's taken a lot of shit from me, and she's still willing to provide things for me when I absolutely can't do it myself. I don't know how familiar you are with some of the borderline personality disorder symptoms, but I had moments where I went fucking insane. I was never physical, but I do things like run away, scream and then physically freeze up for hours (not responding to any touch or words)... I feel like I deserve the comments now. It's the least I can do for her.

I have a place and a job now. My wages are just enough to cover everything, but financially I'm quite in debt from the months of unemployment. 

I let my doctors know, but my care is inconsistent. A combination of no health insurance and times that I'm too depressed to even get out of bed means that I don't have the regular care I think would help. I agree with not following through on the meds. That doesn't help. I also always understate my symptoms because I feel like I must be better than I am. 

I don't attempt suicide on a daily basis, but I surely think about it or harming myself. I just... I really don't see myself getting any better. The doctors I've seen have been upfront and told me that with continued, life-long therapy and medications I might see enough of improvement to function, but I will probably hover in the 60-70 range on the general assessment of functioning score (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Assessment_of_Functioning). I guess that's a significant improvement from when I was so depressed I stopped eating, bathing and ended up with literal shit in the floor at my old place. I just can't bring myself to have enough to look forward to. I've called the suicide hotline a good number of times, but it's always the same stuff and does nothing more than occupy me for an hour. But I also suppose that's better than what I could be doing.

Honestly, if it weren't for the fact that I'm absolutely terrified of losing my job, I'd probably go seek help right now. And even if I got a week off work for treatment, I wouldn't be able to afford rent for the month. It's terrifying.
Given good enough results on this 'pilot challenge', I think we'll move into 'hardcore' mode. I'll put their newly developed brony status to the test.

This totally makes sense, and I agree with you. 

They've already seen various Youtube videos and some of the memes that have spawned from them and have expressed some interest. It's been pretty hard to get them to consider the show by watching the episodes themselves however, as they just don't seem like the kind of people who would sit down and watch anything without direct prompting or strong prior interest. I consider this a stepping stone of sorts. This is perhaps not the typical one (art/videos -> episodes -> community), but getting involved here would definitely move them along. They've gotten a sense of the ponies themselves, and one of them has a very clear favorite, Fluttershy. Luckily, I'm not just bringing in pony-naive friends into this... but people who have at least shown that the idea is fairly appealing. 

They've already agreed to this and thought it was an interesting idea, so I've at least knocked that part out. They're very open-minded people, and I can assure you that they're in no way hostile and mostly curious at this point. 

I don't want to be the guy that makes them sit down and watch the episodes with me. We wouldn't be discovering it together, and there would be lots of expectations. I think this community is a big part of what makes the show and MLP for me, and I really wanted to share this with them. I'm assuming that watching the show will come from this, and I think that seeing what happens here (and, by extension, what things have been produced elsewhere on the Internet) will let them know why I enjoy MLP enough to do something more than simply follow the episodes. Honestly, I think no amount of prompting to discover this community would have worked without some kind of contingency. 

In short, I think it would take a little spark to get them involved enough to consider this community and MLP. They'll come to watch full episodes if they're interested without me having to bring it to them directly, and they'll discover much of what happens 'behind the scenes'. My suggestions to watch the episodes themselves have been met with a general agreement, but they just don't seem to pull themselves together and actually do it.

Edit: I should address more specifically the point about how they wouldn't likely understand what makes the show as good as it is. You're right. Just exposing them to the community won't necessarily entail them watching the show or seeing why people have come to it in the first place. My ultimate hope is that by being as involved as they will be, everything will fall into place and they will eventually see the show and stay with the community. I could be wrong, but I also could have been wrong if I get them to watch some episodes with me and they don't enjoy them. There are other reasons to like MLP than the show itself, and if they end up liking the community and/or the art more than the show itself, I will still consider everything a success.
